path: ServerScriptService/ForgeChecks.server.luau
purpose: Feature: Create executable checks (forge checks --plan) that run a live playtest and assert the telemetry counters: map_built=1, plaza_built=1, themes_built=6, plot_assigned (after claim or the 20s auto-claim), auto_claims, cubes_dropped rising about every 2s, cubes_collected rising, cashin_fx_sent>0, and Cash rising. Also assert that there are no output errors or warnings and that cubes_dropped stays 0 before a claim. Run them, then hand any failing check to the fixer. Keep existing counter names unchanged. -- Studio-only runner (returns immediately unless RunService:IsStudio()) that executes the plan from ForgeChecksPlan. It subscribes to LogService.MessageOut from the start and records Error and Warning entries, ignoring lines that start with its own '[ForgeCheck]' prefix. It waits for the first player and for map_built, plaza_built and themes_built, then snapshots telemetry through ForgeTelemetry.get/snapshot. During the pre-claim window it samples cubes_dropped and plot_assigned and records whether cubes_dropped stayed 0 before any claim. Claim phase: in 'auto' mode it waits for the 20s auto-claim and asserts plot_assigned and auto_claims rose. In 'gate' mode (Workspace attribute ForgeCheckMode='gate') it pivots the player's character onto the first unclaimed gate part to trigger the real Touched claim and asserts plots_claimed and plot_assigned rose. After the claim it samples cubes_dropped, cubes_collected and the player's leaderstats Cash every 2.5s for about 4 windows, then checks cashin_fx_sent>0 and the Output log. For each check it prints one line, '[ForgeCheck] PASS <id>' or '[ForgeCheck] FAIL <id> expected=<..> actual=<..>' (via print, never warn), then a final single line '[ForgeCheck] RESULT {json}' with {passed, failed, failures:[{id, expected, actual}]} that the CLI parses to hand each failing check to the fixer. It sets Workspace attribute ForgeChecksDone=true when finished. It only reads game state and never mutates cash, plots or existing counters. It bumps only its own counters 'checks_passed' and 'checks_failed' with ForgeTelemetry.count. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: checks_passed, checks_failed.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/ForgeChecksPlan.luau, ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau

```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeChecksPlan: pure data describing the live playtest check plan.
-- No services, no side effects. The runner reads `timing`, `checks`, and `counters`,
-- and may call `evaluate` (a pure function) to judge each check.

local Plan = {}

Plan.version = 1

-- 'auto' = rely on the auto-claim fallback; 'gate' = the runner walks onto a claim gate.
Plan.claimMode = "auto"

Plan.timing = {
	settleSeconds = 3,       -- wait after startup before the first observation
	preClaimWindow = 8,      -- observe the plaza before any claim (shorter than the auto-claim delay)
	autoClaimSeconds = 20,   -- spec auto-claim delay (the pre-claim window must stay below it)
	sampleInterval = 2.5,    -- seconds between samples after the claim
	maxRunSeconds = 50,      -- hard cap on the whole run
	minWindowsAfterClaim = 2, -- rising_windows needs at least this many full windows
}

-- ForgeTelemetry counter names the runner bumps (the server runner calls count()).
Plan.counters = {
	passed = "checks_passed",
	failed = "checks_failed",
}

-- Existing counter names, unchanged.
Plan.checks = {
	{ id = "map_built", kind = "counter_eq", counter = "map_built", expect = 1 },
	{ id = "plaza_built", kind = "counter_eq", counter = "plaza_built", expect = 1 },
	{ id = "themes_built", kind = "counter_eq", counter = "themes_built", expect = 6 },
	{ id = "zero_before_claim", kind = "zero_before_claim", counter = "cubes_dropped", expect = 0, guard = "plot_assigned" },
	{ id = "plot_assigned", kind = "counter_gte", counter = "plot_assigned", expect = 1 },
	{ id = "auto_claims", kind = "counter_gte", counter = "auto_claims", expect = 1, mode = "auto" },
	{
		id = "cubes_dropped_rising",
		kind = "rising_windows",
		counter = "cubes_dropped",
		-- minGrowth per window; a faster rate (Dropper 2 bought) is fine, so there is no upper bound.
		expect = { minGrowth = 1, windowSeconds = 2.5, maxGrowth = math.huge },
	},
	{ id = "cubes_collected", kind = "counter_gte", counter = "cubes_collected", expect = 1 },
	{ id = "cashin_fx_sent", kind = "counter_gte", counter = "cashin_fx_sent", expect = 1 },
	{ id = "cash_rising", kind = "cash_rising", counter = "Cash", expect = "greater_than_at_claim" },
	{ id = "no_output_errors", kind = "no_output_errors", counter = "output", expect = { errors = 0, warnings = 0 } },
}

local function num(v: any): number
	if type(v) == "number" then
		return v
	end
	return 0
end

-- Pure evaluator. ctx fields:
--   claimMode: string
--   counters: {[string]: number}        final counter values
--   preClaim: {[string]: number}        counter values at the end of the pre-claim window
--   dropSamples: {number}               cubes_dropped sampled at claim time then each interval
--   cashAtClaim, cashNow: number
--   log: { {type: string, message: string} }
-- Returns ok, message.
function Plan.evaluate(check: any, ctx: any): (boolean, string)
	local kind = check.kind
	local counters = ctx.counters or {}

	if check.mode and check.mode ~= ctx.claimMode then
		return true, "skipped (mode " .. tostring(ctx.claimMode) .. ")"
	end

	if kind == "counter_eq" then
		local v = num(counters[check.counter])
		return v == check.expect, string.format("%s=%s expected %s", check.counter, tostring(v), tostring(check.expect))
	elseif kind == "counter_gte" then
		local v = num(counters[check.counter])
		return v >= check.expect, string.format("%s=%s expected >=%s", check.counter, tostring(v), tostring(check.expect))
	elseif kind == "zero_before_claim" then
		local pre = ctx.preClaim or {}
		if num(pre[check.guard]) > 0 then
			return true, "claim already happened before observation; not testable"
		end
		local v = num(pre[check.counter])
		return v == check.expect, string.format("%s=%s before claim", check.counter, tostring(v))
	elseif kind == "rising_windows" then
		local s = ctx.dropSamples or {}
		local windows = #s - 1
		local minWindows = Plan.timing.minWindowsAfterClaim
		if windows < minWindows then
			return false, string.format("only %d windows sampled, need %d", math.max(windows, 0), minWindows)
		end
		for i = 2, #s do
			local growth = num(s[i]) - num(s[i - 1])
			if growth < check.expect.minGrowth then
				return false, string.format("window %d grew %d (<%d)", i - 1, growth, check.expect.minGrowth)
			end
		end
		return true, string.format("%d windows all rising", windows)
	elseif kind == "cash_rising" then
		local a, b = num(ctx.cashAtClaim), num(ctx.cashNow)
		return b > a, string.format("Cash %s -> %s", tostring(a), tostring(b))
	elseif kind == "no_output_errors" then
		local errs, warns = 0, 0
		for _, entry in ipairs(ctx.log or {}) do
			local t = tostring(entry.type)
			if string.find(t, "Error") then
				errs += 1
			elseif string.find(t, "Warning") then
				warns += 1
			end
		end
		local ok = errs <= check.expect.errors and warns <= check.expect.warnings
		return ok, string.format("%d errors, %d warnings", errs, warns)
	end

	return false, "unknown check kind: " .. tostring(kind)
end

return Plan
```

### ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry
```

# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~10-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza.
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeChecks: Studio-only live playtest runner. Executes ForgeChecksPlan and prints PASS/FAIL lines.
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
if not RunService:IsStudio() then
	return
end

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local LogService = game:GetService("LogService")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local Plan = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeChecksPlan", 10))
local Telemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry", 10))

local PREFIX = "[ForgeCheck]"
local startClock = os.clock()
local deadline = startClock + Plan.timing.maxRunSeconds

-- Output log capture (from the very start)
local logEntries: { { type: string, message: string } } = {}
LogService.MessageOut:Connect(function(message: string, messageType: Enum.MessageType)
	if string.sub(message, 1, #PREFIX) == PREFIX then
		return
	end
	if messageType == Enum.MessageType.MessageError or messageType == Enum.MessageType.MessageWarning then
		table.insert(logEntries, { type = messageType.Name, message = message })
	end
end)

local function num(v: any): number
	if type(v) == "number" then
		return v
	end
	return 0
end

local function describe(v: any): string
	if type(v) == "table" then
		local keys = {}
		for k in pairs(v) do
			table.insert(keys, tostring(k))
		end
		table.sort(keys)
		local parts = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(keys) do
			table.insert(parts, k .. "=" .. tostring((v :: any)[k]))
		end
		return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
	end
	return tostring(v)
end

local function getCash(player: Player?): number
	if not player then
		return 0
	end
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local cash = ls and ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if cash and (cash:IsA("IntValue") or cash:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return (cash :: NumberValue).Value
	end
	return 0
end

-- Observation state
local preClaim: { [string]: number }? = nil
local dropSamples: { number } = {}
local collectedSamples: { number } = {}
local cashAtClaim = 0
local maxCash = 0
local player: Player? = nil

local function observe(): { [string]: number }
	local c = Telemetry.get()
	if preClaim == nil or num(preClaim["plot_assigned"]) == 0 then
		preClaim = c
	end
	maxCash = math.max(maxCash, getCash(player))
	return c
end

local function pause(seconds: number)
	local untilT = os.clock() + seconds
	while os.clock() < untilT and os.clock() < deadline do
		observe()
		task.wait(0.25)
	end
end

local function waitUntil(cond: () -> boolean, timeout: number): boolean
	local untilT = math.min(os.clock() + timeout, deadline)
	while os.clock() < untilT do
		observe()
		if cond() then
			return true
		end
		task.wait(0.25)
	end
	return cond()
end

local function findGate(): BasePart?
	for _, d in ipairs(workspace:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") and string.find(string.lower(d.Name), "gate") and d.Transparency < 1 and d.CanTouch then
			return d
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local claimMode: string = Plan.claimMode
if workspace:GetAttribute("ForgeCheckMode") == "gate" then
	claimMode = "gate"
end

local function claimed(): boolean
	return num(Telemetry.get()["plot_assigned"]) >= 1
end

local function run()
	-- wait for first player
	waitUntil(function()
		return #Players:GetPlayers() > 0
	end, 30)
	player = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
	if player and not player.Character then
		waitUntil(function()
			return player ~= nil and player.Character ~= nil
		end, 10)
	end

	-- wait for the build counters
	waitUntil(function()
		local c = Telemetry.get()
		return num(c["map_built"]) >= 1 and num(c["plaza_built"]) >= 1 and num(c["themes_built"]) >= 6
	end, 20)

	pause(Plan.timing.settleSeconds)
	pause(Plan.timing.preClaimWindow)

	-- claim phase
	if claimMode == "gate" then
		local untilT = os.clock() + 15
		while not claimed() and os.clock() < untilT and os.clock() < deadline do
			local gate = findGate()
			local char = player and player.Character
			if gate and char then
				char:PivotTo(gate.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0))
			end
			waitUntil(claimed, 3)
		end
	else
		waitUntil(claimed, Plan.timing.autoClaimSeconds + 5)
	end

	-- sampling after the claim
	local c0 = observe()
	cashAtClaim = getCash(player)
	maxCash = math.max(maxCash, cashAtClaim)
	table.insert(dropSamples, num(c0["cubes_dropped"]))
	table.insert(collectedSamples, num(c0["cubes_collected"]))
	for _ = 1, 4 do
		if os.clock() >= deadline then
			break
		end
		pause(Plan.timing.sampleInterval)
		local c = observe()
		table.insert(dropSamples, num(c["cubes_dropped"]))
		table.insert(collectedSamples, num(c["cubes_collected"]))
	end
end

local runnerError: string? = nil
local ok, err = pcall(run)
if not ok then
	runnerError = tostring(err)
end

-- Evaluate
local finalCounters = Telemetry.get()
local ctx = {
	claimMode = claimMode,
	counters = finalCounters,
	preClaim = preClaim or finalCounters,
	dropSamples = dropSamples,
	collectedSamples = collectedSamples,
	cashAtClaim = cashAtClaim,
	cashNow = maxCash,
	log = logEntries,
}

local checks: { any } = {}
for _, check in ipairs(Plan.checks) do
	table.insert(checks, check)
end
if claimMode == "gate" then
	table.insert(checks, { id = "plots_claimed", kind = "counter_gte", counter = "plots_claimed", expect = 1 })
end

local passed = 0
local failures: { { id: string, expected: string, actual: string } } = {}

for _, check in ipairs(checks) do
	local pass, message = Plan.evaluate(check, ctx)
	if pass then
		passed += 1
		Telemetry.count(Plan.counters.passed, 1)
		print(string.format("%s PASS %s", PREFIX, check.id))
	else
		local expected = describe(check.expect)
		table.insert(failures, { id = check.id, expected = expected, actual = message })
		Telemetry.count(Plan.counters.failed, 1)
		print(string.format("%s FAIL %s expected=%s actual=%s", PREFIX, check.id, expected, message))
	end
end

if runnerError then
	table.insert(failures, { id = "runner_error", expected = "no error", actual = runnerError })
	Telemetry.count(Plan.counters.failed, 1)
	print(string.format("%s FAIL runner_error expected=no error actual=%s", PREFIX, runnerError))
end

local encOk, json = pcall(function()
	return HttpService:JSONEncode({ passed = passed, failed = #failures, failures = failures })
end)
if not encOk then
	json = string.format('{"passed":%d,"failed":%d,"failures":[]}', passed, #failures)
end
print(string.format("%s RESULT %s", PREFIX, json))

workspace:SetAttribute("ForgeChecksDone", true)
```
